title: Evacuation Arrangements
text: “Working from that premise, I’d like to decide how we proceed. First, we recover the king, Melty-chan, Filo, and the slave children. After that, I’m thinking we deal with the group occupying the castle—does Your Majesty share that view?”
“Yes.”

“Well, personally, I’d be fine with Naofumi-san’s group recovering the king while Motoyasu-san and I march straight into the castle town, storm the castle, and knock some sense into every one of those high-and-mighty humans, one by one, cleaning house. This world’s garbage would just vanish, wouldn’t it?”
For some reason I’d been folded into Itsuki’s plan. If it were Father giving the order, I say, I wouldn’t mind doing it—but why must I go on a rampage with Itsuki of all people!?

“Isn’t announcing a mass slaughter like that to Her Majesty a bit much? Sorry about this. Ever since Itsuki got turned into this form, despite being a Hero, he went through some horrific experience as a slave, and it’s left him consumed by a desire for revenge.”
“…All we can do is apologize. Everything stems from our nation’s religion and from what Aultcray brought about. All I can do is pray for… generous mercy.”
The Queen, sensing the circumstances behind Itsuki’s state, apologized over and over. Crocodile Guy let out a sigh at the sight of Itsuki.

“I do think we’ll end up storming the castle eventually. But we should aim for as few casualties as possible—the citizens are just being manipulated, after all. If the Queen and the King make a proper declaration, things should settle down.”
“I wonder about that. If there’s some other solution, I’d love to hear it.”

…There wasn’t exactly none, I say. In the very first world, Father had cleverly cornered the Three Heroes Church into ruin by winning the people’s support. It had gone much the same way in this loop, when Father operated within Melromarc—though a rather violent conflict had broken out along the way. And in that conflict, you, the figurehead, got cornered, indeed. And that was when Éclair died in prison. This is what happens when you don’t exactly do good deeds. It had been a case of getting neatly manipulated by the Three Heroes Church. And right on cue, the Queen turned to look at Ren. Ren promptly hid further behind Father.
“The citizens support Amaki-sama. Once this matter is resolved, might we ask for Amaki-sama’s cooperation?”
“Ugh… ah, no… that’s not me, it’s… no… hmph. I’ll think about it.”
“Ren… what, are you getting cold feet from your social anxiety or something?”
“But Naofumi! That’s… gah…”

It seemed to be one of those things he couldn’t bring himself to say, indeed. It was all thanks to Rafumi’s efforts. Ren had ended up in a position much like Father’s evaluation back when Father had remained in Melromarc—currently serving as Melromarc’s hope. Rafumi too had maneuvered skillfully, maintaining a position just barely out of the Three Heroes Church’s crosshairs, indeed. At this rate, it looked like things were heading toward Ren getting engaged to Fiancée as a way to secure Melromarc’s survival. Ha! What a chance, I say! In this loop, once Fiancée got engaged to Ren, Filo-tan would open right up.
“Motoyasu… don’t tell me you exposed everything and turned me back just for this!”
“Whatever do you mean? I merely couldn’t stand Rival getting carried away with itself, I say.”
“Well, that’s about right for Motoyasu-kun. Ren, Motoyasu-kun isn’t clever enough for that.”
“I suppose not. If you want someone to blame, it’d be Gaelion-san, I’d say.”
“Damn it! That dragon, betraying me like that! I’ll never forgive it!”
That is simply the sort of creature a dragon is, I say. Stealing Father away from me was an atrocity I could never forgive, no matter what.
“Well, in any case, let’s proceed with that plan for now… the question is whether we can link up smoothly with that king. And where exactly is he right now with Melty-chan and the others?”
Right, Father was checking Filo-tan’s Monster Seal for a signal.
“Well, either way, Your Majesty, please persuade the king. As for that other troublesome princess of yours…”
He was driving the nail in about the matter concerning the Crimson Swine too.

“…As for that, she has already been apprehended in Faubrey and is currently being transported back. She should arrive around the time this current matter is resolved. Honestly… why on earth would she waltz right into Faubrey?”
The Queen let out a sigh. Ah, so it seemed the Crimson Swine had been caught. Just as expected, she’d probably gone off to meet with Takt or someone, plotting all sorts of mischief.
“Naturally, she will be held accountable for triggering this incident and attempting to sow discord among the Heroes for her own selfish ends, so please bear with us a little longer.”
“There’s no denying there are all sorts of problems with her, but if anything, isn’t her upbringing the real cause?”

Itsuki’s interrogation turned toward the Queen. No doubt, in Itsuki’s analysis, the Crimson Swine had been raised into human supremacism by Trash and the Queen’s upbringing. The Crimson Swine was a pig by nature, I say. The very fact that she shared blood with Fiancée and the Queen was itself a mystery.
“We disciplined her strictly, time and again, but her problematic behavior never improved. She is a disgrace of a daughter.”
“Itsuki, just looking at Melty-chan, you can tell it’s that princess’s own personal problem.”
“I suppose I’ll leave it at that. Well… I did get to watch, hand clamped on her head, the exact moment she illegally fired off that spell. I remember the look on her face then, you know?”
Itsuki seemed to be holding quite the grudge, I say. And taking a jab at Father too! Father did nothing wrong, I say.
“Well then, shall we start the operation? Your Majesty, please accompany us. We’ll protect you no matter what happens, so rest assured… Eclair-san, I’m counting on you too.”
“Of course. Whatever happens, I will protect Her Majesty.”
“Filo-tan, coming your way now-zo!”

And so, with the Queen in tow, we infiltrated Melromarc to link up with Trash. Stepping outside the building, we found Rafumi and Rival already waiting, primed and ready to depart. Don’t you two come along! I wanted to say, but they’d ended up joining us regardless. How infuriating, I say. If only Rival hadn’t come back, I wouldn’t have had to reveal that I was an usaunny, and my request would’ve gone through. And so, using Filo-tan’s Monster Seal as our guide while also keeping an eye on Rafumi, we made our way to Trash’s hideout.
…A mole’s den, I say.
“Of all places, they came here.”
It was the mole den that Itsuki’s mole friend had mentioned—the one with an escape route out of Melromarc.
“Ha, quite the fateful place, isn’t it? But it’s rather ironic that of all places, the anti-Demi-Human king would flee here.”
Itsuki let out a dry laugh.
“Well, since Filo and Melty-chan have picked up bits of the situation on our end, it might make sense that things led to them hiding out here.”
“Indeed…”
Éclair too seemed conflicted, nodding along with Father’s words.
“What is this place?”

“Your Majesty, my father apparently prepared this in case something happened in Melromarc—a hidden route for Demi-Humans and Beastmen to flee the clutches of slave hunters and escape to another country.”

“I see… Under my family’s usual policy, this would ordinarily warrant severe punishment. But I have no intention of punishing anyone over this matter. That is how much I had come to place my hopes in Seaetto.”
The Queen seemed inclined to turn a blind eye toward the passage hidden in the mole’s den.
“More than anything, if it’s also been of help to Aultcray and the others, then I suppose we ought to view that as a good thing.”
“I am grateful for Your Majesty’s generous judgment.”
Éclair bowed her thanks at the Queen’s words.
“Well, even now I still come by sometimes, helping arrange evacuations for Demi-Humans and Beastmen who want to flee Melromarc.”
So Itsuki testified that he too dropped by occasionally to check on the place. Well, it was a mole’s den after all. Since Itsuki had lived here too, it was probably a familiar dwelling to him by now.
“The concern is whether Aultcray might have set traps, same as with Itsuki’s case…”
“Doesn’t seem to be any problem here.”
“Master—!”
Oh! Filo-tan came pattering toward us with Fiancée riding on her back.
“Filo-taaan!”
I too dashed forward, about to leap at approaching Filo-tan, when Father grabbed me by the scruff of my neck.
